citations.quote: For tax year 2025 and each year thereafter, the credit is one hundred fifty-five dollars ($155).
citations.source: Idaho Code § 63-3024A, Food Tax Credits and Refunds

citations.quote: If taxes due are less than the total credit allowed, the taxpayer shall be paid a refund equal to the balance of the unused credit.
citations.source: Idaho Code § 63-3024A, Food Tax Credits and Refunds

citations.quote: the credit or refund allowed under this section shall be in proportion to the number of months of the year in which no assistance was received.
citations.source: Idaho Code § 63-3024A, Food Tax Credits and Refunds

summary: Under Idaho Code § 63-3024A, each full-year resident who files gets a food tax credit (formerly the grocery credit) of $155 per personal exemption "for tax year 2025 and each year thereafter." Any part of the credit that exceeds the tax due is paid as a refund. The credit has no income limit. It is prorated only for months in which the filer received SNAP, and none is listed here. The engine counted $155 for one person over 12 qualifying months, which matches the statute. The 0 consensus wrongly assumed the credit is nonrefundable or income-limited, and stage 1 was right.
